explanation:
[EFFECT] Humidity has a non-monotonic effect on predicted bike demand. At extremely low humidity (below about 5%), the model strongly suppresses demand. Demand is boosted slightly at low-to-moderate humidity levels (roughly 5–40% relative humidity), where the contribution peaks at around +0.1 in log space. As humidity rises above ~40%, the contribution steadily declines, becoming noticeably negative above about 70–80%, reaching roughly -0.25 to -0.30 at the highest humidity levels.

[IMPORTANCE] With an importance score of 0.083 and a rank of 5th out of 9 features, humidity has a moderate influence on predicted demand — meaningful, but less impactful than the top drivers such as hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION] On high-humidity days (above ~70–80% relative humidity), plan for meaningfully reduced ridership and consider redistributing staff or bikes accordingly, while maintaining fuller availability during comfortable, low-to-moderate humidity conditions when demand is at its highest.
